seed: Under a recording sits a row of eight pictures with no word beside any of them, and until now resting on one raised the system help tag: a box macOS draws in its own style, on its own schedule, looking like nothing else in Photonz. The person using it said so twice: "tooltips don't look like any other tooltip. I don't know what the buttons do." This walk proves the row now answers in the app's OWN tooltip, the same plate a tool in the floating bar answers with, and that the pictures are the app's own: Trim wears the Trim TOOL's glyph instead of scissors, and Export wears an arrow going out instead of the one that means bringing a file in.

steps.note: THE STANDARD to measure the row against: the Crop tool in the floating bar, resting. One short name on a dark slate plate with a blunted beak, the key printed quieter under it. Every picture below has to look like this one

the row as it stands on an untouched recording: trim, crop, copy, export, with the split beside them and the transport in the middle. Save, undo and the trash are not drawn because there is nothing yet to save, take back or throw away

THE TEST: the same plate as step 0, over the button that used to wear scissors. The picture is timeline.selection, which is what the Trim TOOL wears in the picture editor and what the mock's ic-trim draws: a clip with an in point and an out point
THE TEST: the arrow now leaves the tray. It used to be an arrow going down INTO one, which is the picture of bringing a file in, and it sat in the same row as Save's own down arrow
the transport answers the same way, and names the key in the app's own notation
two seconds in, the recording still one whole piece: the split is live and names the key that does the same thing
the cut lands and the row grows by three: save, undo and the trash. Eight pictures, and every one of them answers

THE TEST: the playhead is sitting ON the join it just made, and a second cut in the same place is not a thing, so the button is dimmed. Dimmed, it still answers with its name and its key, instead of being a grey picture that does nothing and explains nothing
undo names the edit it would take back rather than saying Undo at nothing, and prints its key
THE TEST: the same plate in light appearance. The bar under a recording is dark chrome either way, so the tooltip has to read against it in both
